text: 50-year-old female. text: Past medical history: Hypertension, osteoarthritis. Social history: Has started hiking in the woods on weekends. No relevant travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blisters are indeed very fragile and rupture easily, leaving behind painful erosions rather than intact bullae, and I have noticed some crusting around my lips. I have not observed any significant scarring, but the pain in my mouth makes eating very difficult.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the fragile blisters, severe oral ulcers, and recent initiation of captopril, this presentation is highly suggestive of drug-induced pemphigus vulgaris. I will now order a skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence to confirm the diagnosis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Histopathology shows acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation. Direct immunofluorescence reveals intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results confirm Pemphigus vulgaris, characterized by acantholysis and intercellular IgG deposition. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus vulgaris
